title: Mark 11:27–33
context: The temple authorities demand to know by what authority Jesus acts. He answers with a question about John’s baptism: from heaven or from men? Trapped between their unbelief and their fear of the crowd, they plead ignorance, and Jesus declines to answer them. Arminian and Reformed readers agree the passage exposes leaders unwilling to follow the truth they already have.

verses.text: They came again to Jerusalem, and as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to him,
verses.arminianNotes: In the temple the chief priests, scribes, and elders approach him. Arminian and Reformed readers agree these represent the Sanhedrin’s leadership.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the very groups Jesus predicted would reject him (Mark 8:31) now confront him.

verses.text: and they began saying to him, “By what authority do you do these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?”
verses.arminianNotes: By what authority do you do these things, and who gave it to you? Arminian and Reformed readers agree these things include the temple action.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the question of Jesus’ authority is central to Mark’s Gospel.

verses.text: Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
verses.arminianNotes: Jesus answers with one question of his own. Arminian and Reformed readers agree this is a recognized teaching method that exposes motives.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Jesus’ wisdom in refusing a trap.

verses.text: The baptism of John—was it from heaven, or from men? Answer me.”
verses.arminianNotes: Was John’s baptism from heaven or from men? Arminian and Reformed readers agree the question links Jesus’ authority with John’s witness to him.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that accepting John meant accepting the one he announced.

verses.text: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we should say, ‘From heaven;’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
verses.arminianNotes: They reason that if they say from heaven, he will ask why they did not believe John. Arminian readers note that they reason pragmatically rather than seeking truth.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see hearts unwilling to submit, more concerned with the consequences than with the truth.

verses.text: If we should say, ‘From men’”—they feared the people, for all held John to really be a prophet.
verses.arminianNotes: If from men, they fear the people, who held John to be a prophet. Arminian and Reformed readers agree fear of the crowd controls them.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the fear of man as a snare (Proverbs 29:25).

verses.text: They answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
verses.arminianNotes: They say we don’t know, and Jesus refuses to tell them his authority. Arminian and Reformed readers agree that those who refuse light already given do not receive more.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the refusal exposes their unbelief while the parable that follows answers the question indirectly.
